decision: NO_ADVANCEMENT: retain all existing proof observations and positive-timeout direct fallback. No implementation, benchmark or qualification claim follows this assessment.

broadDefaultComposition.proposedChange: Run full Stage10 only at default-native public composition opening/closing, while opaque providers retain the existing internal checks.
broadDefaultComposition.assessment: Not established as contract preserving. It removes existing live native observation points even if generic provider negatives remain on a slow path.

concreteBarriers.evidence: source-stage10.mjs forwards preload methods via values=>actual.git[name](values); the inner method is dynamically obtained. Freezing or branding an outer wrapper does not seal the referenced provider graph or mutable method tables.

concreteBarriers.barrier: The default native transport still exposes ambient effects
concreteBarriers.evidence: runtimeNativeGit snapshots live process.env and options; the broker executes PATH-resolved Git with each request environment. Git configuration, fsmonitor/promisor/helper execution and mutable module/builtin dependencies are not made pure by a function brand.

concreteBarriers.barrier: Pure JavaScript does not freeze live workspace state
concreteBarriers.evidence: Even with no synchronous JS callback, another process can move HEAD/index/root and restore it between the proposed public fences. An original internal native observation can detect an excursion that the reduced observation set misses.

concreteBarriers.barrier: Existing negative tests are necessary but insufficient for specialization
concreteBarriers.evidence: Sending explicitly wrapped/opaque providers through the old path preserves those cases but does not prove the fast default path retains its original native mutation/refusal contract. Freezing formerly mutable exported methods would itself change supported behavior.

broadDefaultComposition.requiredBeforeAnyDifferentContract: A separately audited internal kernel would need transitive capability/intrinsic/IO proofs and an explicit treatment of concurrent filesystem/configuration effects. That is a new proof contract/backend design, not an authorized narrow removal of existing checks. No such redesign is proposed.

positiveTimeoutRouting.assessment: Exact positive-timeout brokering is not inherently impossible, but cannot be obtained by only lifting requestFor rejection. Existing timeout+5000 main watchdog would change ignored-SIGTERM behavior; Node22 timeout/error/overflow precedence, partial bytes, send-once signal then wait/drain, and original outer-PGID cleanup need explicit equivalence work. No such work is justified as the next recovery guess by the measured opportunity.
positiveTimeoutRouting.criticalDistinction: The approximately1.35s direct opening/closing total includes zero-timeout common-dir, origin, raw state and HEAD work. Only approximately354ms is positive-timeout batch work, and its Git execution remains necessary; achievable savings are below that ceiling.
positiveTimeoutRouting.memoryRisk: Routing the96.5MB collection blob output through the fixed shared output buffer touches an additional large main-process mapping; that work occurs outside the API timer but can enlarge later direct-fork RSS.
positiveTimeoutRouting.decision: Do not run the proposed positive-timeout advisory variant or implement it. Preserve current native positive-timeout fallback and all existing tests/checks.

performanceStatus: Original five-second API qualification remains failed. This assessment does not relax the150s source child,65s shortest wrapper,20min source-unit job or any other original gate.
